name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q01 - Matching contraceptive categories with their examples

questiontext.text:
Match the contraceptive categories with their respective examples and select the correct combination:

List I List II
(a) Non-medicated IUD (i) Multiload 375
(b) Copper-releasing IUD (ii) Coitus interruptus
(c) Hormone-releasing IUD (iii) Lippes loop
(d) Natural method (iv) LNG-20

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraceptive methods are grouped into natural/traditional methods, barrier methods, intrauterine devices (IUDs), oral contraceptives, injectables, implants, and surgical methods. IUDs are further divided into non-medicated, copper-releasing, and hormone-releasing types.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD, so (a) pairs with (iii). Multiload 375 (along with CuT and Cu7) is a copper-releasing IUD, so (b) pairs with (i). LNG-20 (along with Progestasert) is a hormone-releasing IUD, so (c) pairs with (iv). Coitus interruptus (withdrawal) is a natural/traditional method of contraception, so (d) pairs with (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q02 - Matching contraceptive methods with their mechanisms of action

questiontext.text:
Match the contraceptive methods with their primary modes of action and choose the correct set of pairs:

List I List II
(a) Condoms (i) Blocks sperm transport through the vas deferens
(b) Progestasert (ii) Prevents ejaculated semen from entering the female reproductive tract
(c) Vasectomy (iii) Inhibits ovulation and implantation and alters cervical mucus
(d) Oral pills (iv) Makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different contraceptive methods prevent conception through distinct mechanisms: physical barriers prevent gamete meeting, hormone-releasing IUDs alter uterine and cervical receptivity, surgical methods block gamete transport, and oral pills suppress ovulation and implantation.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
Condoms are thin rubber/latex sheaths that prevent ejaculated semen from entering the female reproductive tract, so (a) pairs with (ii). Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD that makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms, so (b) pairs with (iv). Vasectomy is a male surgical sterilisation method that cuts or ties the vas deferens to block sperm transport, so (c) pairs with (i). Oral pills contain progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations that inhibit ovulation and implantation while altering cervical mucus quality, so (d) pairs with (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q03 - Matching assisted reproductive technologies with their procedures

questiontext.text:
Match the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) with their corresponding procedures:

List I List II
(a) ZIFT (i) Transfer of embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
(b) IUT (ii) Direct injection of a sperm into the ovum in the laboratory
(c) GIFT (iii) Transfer of zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
(d) ICSI (iv) Transfer of a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a recipient female

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Assisted reproductive technologies (ART) assist infertile couples through specialised procedures involving gamete or embryo handling in the laboratory and transfer into the female reproductive tract.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transferring the zygote or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube, so (a) pairs with (iii). IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) involves transferring embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus, so (b) pairs with (i). GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transferring an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, so (c) pairs with (iv). ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a laboratory procedure where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum, so (d) pairs with (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q04 - Matching reproductive health initiatives and medical techniques

questiontext.text:
Match the reproductive health initiatives and techniques with their associated facts in India:

List I List II
(a) Family planning programme (i) Legalised in 1971 with strict conditions to prevent misuse
(b) Saheli (ii) Initiated at a national level in 1951
(c) Medical Termination of Pregnancy (iii) Analyses foetal cells in amniotic fluid for genetic disorders
(d) Amniocentesis (iv) Non-steroidal once-a-week oral pill developed at CDRI, Lucknow

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India implemented national programmes, legislative acts, and indigenous research initiatives to promote reproductive health and check population growth and female foeticide.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
India initiated family planning programmes at the national level in 1951, so (a) pairs with (ii). Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week oral contraceptive developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow, so (b) pairs with (iv). The Government of India legalised Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid misuse, so (c) pairs with (i). Amniocentesis involves taking amniotic fluid of the developing foetus to analyse foetal cells and dissolved substances for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anaemia, so (d) pairs with (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q05 - Matching barrier and natural contraceptives with key features

questiontext.text:
Match the contraceptive methods with their specific features:

List I List II
(a) Nirodh (i) Reusable rubber barrier inserted to cover the cervix during coitus
(b) Diaphragm (ii) Effective up to a maximum period of six months following parturition
(c) Lactational amenorrhea (iii) Avoiding coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
(d) Periodic abstinence (iv) Disposable male condom that also protects against STIs and AIDS

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Barrier and natural contraceptive methods prevent fertilisation without altering hormonal levels, but differ in reusability, timing, and protection against sexually transmitted infections.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
Nirodh is a popular brand of disposable condom for males that prevents conception and offers the additional benefit of protecting against STIs and AIDS, so (a) pairs with (iv). Diaphragms (along with cervical caps and vaults) are reusable rubber barriers inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus, so (b) pairs with (i). Lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition during intense lactation, so (c) pairs with (ii). Periodic abstinence requires couples to avoid coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation is expected, so (d) pairs with (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q06 - Matching sexually transmitted infections with clinical characteristics

questiontext.text:
Match the items related to Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) with their correct clinical or epidemiological details:

List I List II
(a) Hepatitis-B and HIV (i) Completely curable if detected early and treated properly
(b) Gonorrhoea and Syphilis (ii) Age group reported to have very high incidence of STIs
(c) Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) (iii) Not completely curable; can spread via shared needles or blood transfusion
(d) 15–24 years (iv) Late complication of untreated STIs along with ectopic pregnancy and infertility

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexually transmitted infections vary in their transmission routes, curability, high-risk age groups, and long-term complications if left untreated.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
Hepatitis-B and HIV (along with genital herpes) are not completely curable, and hepatitis-B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles, surgical instruments, blood transfusion, or from an infected mother to the foetus, so (a) pairs with (iii). Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV, other STIs such as gonorrhoea and syphilis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly, so (b) pairs with (i). Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is a serious late complication of untreated STIs, alongside abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, and reproductive tract cancer, so (c) pairs with (iv). The incidence of STIs is reported to be very high among persons in the 15–24 years age group, so (d) pairs with (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCH_Q07 - Matching demographic parameters and statutory provisions in India

questiontext.text:
Match the demographic parameters and statutory provisions with their corresponding figures or rules in India:

List I List II
(a) Indian population in May 2011 (i) 18 years for females and 21 years for males
(b) Population growth rate (2011 census) (ii) Crossed 1.2 billion mark
(c) Statutory marriageable age (iii) Opinion of two registered medical practitioners required between 12 and 24 weeks
(d) MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 (iv) Less than 2 per cent (20/1000/year)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Population stabilisation and safe abortion in India are tracked through census demographic indicators and regulated through statutory age and medical practitioner requirements.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
India's population crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011, so (a) pairs with (ii). According to the 2011 census report, India's population growth rate was less than 2 per cent, i.e., 20/1000/year, so (b) pairs with (iv). The statutory marriageable age was raised to 18 years for females and 21 years for males to help check population growth, so (c) pairs with (i). Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2017, if a pregnancy has lasted more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must be of the opinion that the required grounds exist, so (d) pairs with (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairing is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).
